full_period/cmip6_ensemble_coverage_basi.caption: CMIP6 ensemble availability. Numbers give resolved member counts for each model and scenario; historical counts give unique loaded reference series associated with resolved scenario members. Zero indicates no resolved or loaded member in this ensemble, not necessarily absence from the CMIP6 archive. Availability does not guarantee eligibility for every variable, period, or analysis window. Families describe model code genealogy using the mapping attributed to Kuma et al. (2023, doi:10.1029/2022MS003588; Zenodo record 7920408). An asterisk marks a provisional family inferred from institution; ? marks an unknown family. Parentheses identify institution and country where known. Family labels do not imply statistical independence within or between families.

full_period/cmip6_temp_annual_anomaly_ts.caption: CMIP6 projections: trajectory temperature. Ensemble spread across 2 models (equal model weight), not a confidence interval; models from one code family count separately. Bold lines show the median across 2 models, with members averaged first; ribbons span the model range. Black denotes the historical run and scenario colors the future runs; faint traces are individual members. Annual values are unsmoothed, so the range includes year-to-year variability and is not a confidence interval. Each member uses its own 1985–2014 reference mean. Pale shading marks the future analysis windows; the dashed line marks the current year.

full_period/cmip6_temp_annual_overview_b.caption: CMIP6 projections: annual temperature. Absolute annual values are shown above and anomalies relative to each member's 1985–2014 mean below. Temperature and its anomalies are in °C. Thin gray lines show individual historical members and thin scenario-colored lines show individual future members. Thick black lines show historical member medians; thick scenario-colored lines show future member medians. Colored envelopes span the member range, not a confidence interval or an equal-model reduction. The dashed line marks the historical–scenario transition at 2014.5; pale shading marks the future analysis windows. Missing years remain gaps.

period_2036_2065/cmip6_temp_annual_seaso.caption: CMIP6 projections: change temperature. Analysis future WY 2036–2065; analysis reference WY 1985–2014. Configured horizon mid: future 2046–2054, reference 2000–2014. The change-factor CSV uses the configured windows. Seasonal precipitation absolute and percentage changes use rates; the lab's total-based percentages are a documented parity exception. CV uses period integrals. Ensemble spread across 2 models (equal model weight), not a confidence interval; models from one code family count separately. Panels show annual and seasonal changes. Outlined boxes span the model interquartile range where at least 10 models contribute; horizontal bars mark medians and capped vertical lines span the full model range. Faint points show individual models, with members averaged first and horizontal jitter for legibility. Zero indicates no change.

period_2036_2065/cmip6_temp_monthly_clim.caption: CMIP6 projections: seasonal cycle temperature. Reference water years 1985–2014; future water years 2036–2065. Lines show the median monthly climatology across models, with members averaged first. Black denotes the historical reference and colors denote future scenarios. Gray shading spans the historical model range; future spread is shown in the companion monthly-change figure. The historical climatology uses the first displayed scenario's contributing models. Model spread is descriptive and is not a confidence interval.

period_2036_2065/cmip6_temp_monthly_chan.caption: CMIP6 projections: monthly change temperature. Reference water years 1985–2014; future water years 2036–2065. Each panel shows one scenario's monthly changes. Capped lines span the model range, outline boxes show the interquartile range where at least 10 models contribute, and thick horizontal bars show the median. Members are averaged within each model first. Zero indicates no change; precipitation changes are percentages of the reference rate. Model spread is descriptive and is not a confidence interval.

period_2036_2065/cmip6_temp_annual_seaso.caption: CMIP6 interannual variability: variability ratio temperature sd. Future/reference ratios for 2036–2065 relative to 1985–2014. Model spread is descriptive, not a confidence interval. Ratios above 1 indicate increased interannual variability and ratios below 1 indicate decreased variability. Each member is detrended separately within each window; model ratios are geometric means of member ratios and models have equal weight. Outlined boxes show the model interquartile range where at least 10 models contribute, thick bars show the median, capped lines span the model range and faint points show models. Sampling benchmarks are not displayed in this figure. Excluded degenerate ratios: 0; zero-future ratios: 0.

period_2036_2065/cmip6_precip_annual_sea.caption: CMIP6 interannual variability: variability ratio precipitation sd. Future/reference ratios for 2036–2065 relative to 1985–2014. Model spread is descriptive, not a confidence interval. Ratios above 1 indicate increased interannual variability and ratios below 1 indicate decreased variability. Each member is detrended separately within each window; model ratios are geometric means of member ratios and models have equal weight. Precipitation SD is calculated from period mean daily rates; precipitation CV uses detrended SD of period totals divided by their original mean. These aggregations can differ when period lengths vary. CV excludes periods with dry reference or future means. Outlined boxes show the model interquartile range where at least 10 models contribute, thick bars show the median, capped lines span the model range and faint points show models. Sampling benchmarks are not displayed in this figure. Excluded degenerate ratios: 0; zero-future ratios: 0.

period_2036_2065/cmip6_precip_temp_annua.caption: CMIP6 annual mean changes for 2036–2065 relative to 1985–2014. Each point pairs precipitation and temperature changes from the same model and scenario, with members averaged within each model first. Colors identify scenarios. Precipitation changes are percentages of the reference mean; temperature changes are in °C. Zero reference lines indicate no change. The cloud shows descriptive model spread, not probabilities or a confidence region; models from the same code family may be dependent.

CMIP6 sign agreement in annual and monthly mean changes for 2036–2065 relative to 1985–2014. Each model contributes once after averaging its members. Cell signs indicate the sign of the median model change: + denotes increase and − decrease. Counts k/n give the number of models sharing that sign out of the eligible models; darker fills indicate stronger agreement. Blue denotes increase and red decrease. Agreement measures consistency of direction, not change magnitude, a probability, or statistical significance. Models sharing code ancestry are not independent, so model counts need not represent independent lines of evidence.
